newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty gains vs basket, depos edge lower.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty gains vs basket, depos edge lower.

text.p: The zloty recouped some Monday losses against the basket of currencies today as foreigners continued to flock to high yielding Polish treasuries and put upward pressure on the local unit.

Dealers said the central bank, whose interventions pulled the zloty one point lower on Monday, wanted short-term exchange rate volatility to discourage foreign inflows into treasuries, roughly estimated at $50 million on Tuesday.
"There are now two forces on the market, foreign investors who sell dollars, pushing the zloty higher, and the central bank, which knocks it down," said Marcin Stefaniuk from BDK SA.
The zloty closed at 3.31/3.27 percent from the trading band centre, firmer than Monday's 3.09/2.93 percent.
It closed at 2.9430/45 to the dollar, up from 2.9520/50 on Monday and at 1.8138/47 to the mark, also up from 1.8140/60.
Dealers said currency selling dominated at today's fixing which they said signalled that the zloty was likely to edge upward toward 3.5 percent from parity on Wednesday.
The zloty was fixed at an average of 3.36 percent from the dollar and mark central parity rates on Tuesday, stronger than 2.82 percent on Monday and at the end of 1996.

The daily average level of Polish reserve money in December was 34.964 billion zlotys, within the National Bank of Poland's target band of 34.43 to 35.13 billion zlotys, rising by 7.15 billion in 1996 against a planned seven billion zloty rise.

One-day deposit rates eased slightly on Tuesday despite a 393 million zloty NBP-bill sale and a 144 million zloty drainage for seven and 14 days. Overnight rates closed at 21.50/21.70 percent, down from opening's 21.90/22.10 percent.
Tomorrow/next rates closed at 21.63/21.80 percent, down from 21.90/22.15 percent this morning.
